title: 21.5 A Fully Integrated Multi-Phase Voltage Regulator with Enhanced Light-Load-Efficiency Peak of 86%, Featuring an Autonomous Mode Transition from Hard-Switching to Soft-Switching to Discontinuous Conduction Mode in 3nm FinFET CMOS
problem: Fully integrated voltage regulators (FIVRs) face efficiency challenges across the power spectrum: high efficiency at peak power (current surges) but poor efficiency at idle loads; soft-switching and DCM modes reduce ripple but degrade efficiency under high load.
method: 3nm FIVR with autonomous mode transition from hard-switching (high load) to soft-switching to discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) at light load, maintaining droop response while achieving 86% peak light-load efficiency.

title: BiNeuroRAM: Energy-Efficient ReRAM-Based PIM for Accurate Bipolar Spiking Neural Network Acceleration
problem: Existing ReRAM-based neuromorphic accelerators suffer from high sensing power and accuracy degradation when running spiking neural networks, limiting their deployment.
method: BiNeuroRAM uses ReRAM-based processing-in-memory with three innovations: (1) support for spike-tracing bipolar-integrate-and-fire (ST-BIF) neurons enabling higher accuracy; (2) low-power voltage sense amplifier (LPVSA) reducing ReRAM read power by 14.7-58.2x via optimized sensing; (3) asynchronous micro-architecture exploiting event-driven SNN sparsity to maximize throughput.

title: Intel IPU E2200: Second Generation Infrastructure Processing Unit (IPU)
problem: Data center infrastructure requires specialized processing for networking, security, and telemetry offloads; Intel IPU E2200 targets accelerating infrastructure workloads beyond GPU/CPU capability.
method: IPU E2200 integrates a multi-core compute fabric optimized for packet processing and infrastructure workloads, with hardware accelerators for cryptography and telemetry collection, connected via high-speed fabric to enable efficient offloading from general-purpose compute.

title: SYLQ-SV: Scaling Symbolic Execution of Hardware Designs with Query Caching
problem: Symbolic execution of hardware designs (in SystemVerilog) suffers from path explosion, making full security and functional verification intractably expensive. Existing engines lack comprehensive SystemVerilog language support and do not exploit redundancy across SMT queries generated during path exploration.
method: SylQ-SV is a dedicated SystemVerilog symbolic execution engine that caches SMT queries across paths. When the engine encounters a query that is semantically equivalent to a previously solved one, it retrieves the cached result rather than re-invoking the SMT solver, avoiding redundant computation. The engine also provides full SystemVerilog language coverage including SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) to support end-to-end verification of open-source designs.

title: AI Revolution Driven by Memory Technology Innovation
problem: The 'memory wall' phenomenon—the growing mismatch between compute speed and memory bandwidth—is intensifying in the AI era. Conventional memory architectures cannot support the bandwidth, latency, and capacity demands of modern AI algorithms, limiting system performance and algorithm innovation.
method: The abstract outlines that memory companies have been developing multiple solutions over several years to address power, performance, and capacity requirements for AI systems. These technologies are being gradually integrated into products to bridge the memory-compute gap.

title: KernelGPT: Enhanced Kernel Fuzzing via Large Language Models
problem: Kernel fuzzing effectiveness depends critically on syscall specifications that define the syntax and semantics of system calls, but generating these specifications is largely manual work, leaving large numbers of important syscalls uncovered and limiting automated kernel vulnerability discovery.
method: KernelGPT uses large language models to automatically generate and repair syscall specifications for kernel fuzzing. The system prompts an LLM with kernel source code and documentation to synthesize syscall specifications in the format expected by the Syzkaller fuzzer, then uses an iterative refinement loop where fuzzing feedback is fed back to the LLM to repair invalid or incomplete specifications. This LLM-guided specification generation covers previously uncovered syscalls and improves the semantic validity of generated syscall sequences.

title: Late Breaking Results: The Hidden Risks of Activation Duration in PLPUFs
problem: Pseudo Linear Feedback Shift Register PUF (PLPUF) security depends critically on activation duration selection, but improper choices compromise security significantly.
method: Analyzes linear dependency between responses of different PLPUF pairs as function of activation duration. Identifies that certain activation durations lead to high predictability (96%) of responses.

title: Accelerating Simulation of Quantum Circuits under Noise via Computational Reuse
problem: Noisy quantum circuit simulation on HPC systems is prohibitively slow because simulators must iteratively re-execute nearly identical circuits thousands of times across different noise model trials, recomputing the same intermediate quantum states from scratch each time.
method: TQSim (Tree-Based Quantum Circuit Simulation) dynamically partitions a quantum circuit into subcircuits and constructs a tree of intermediate results that can be reused across different noisy simulation trials. The system identifies which subcircuit branches diverge due to noise injection and reuses cached intermediate density matrix or statevector results for the converging branches, avoiding redundant re-simulation. The approach is designed for multi-node distributed HPC setups with tight fidelity bounds on the approximation.

title: LMM-IR: Large-Scale Netlist-Aware Multimodal Framework for Static IR-Drop Prediction
problem: Static IR drop analysis is a critical bottleneck in chip design, requiring hours of computation per iteration; iterative refinement for violations exacerbates computational burden, making fast prediction essential.
method: Proposes multimodal approach processing SPICE netlists via large-scale netlist transformer (LNT) that represents topology as 3D point clouds for efficient handling of designs with hundreds of thousands to millions of nodes. Encodes netlists (SPICE files) and imagery as latent features fed to unified model for voltage drop prediction. Integrates multimodal data for complementary predictions.

title: CIMFlow: An Integrated Framework for Systematic Design and Evaluation of Digital CIM Architectures
problem: Digital compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures promise DNN acceleration by addressing the memory wall, but lack comprehensive design and evaluation frameworks that cover both software (compilation) and hardware design spaces, and fail to address capacity constraints inherent in CIM systems.
method: CIMFlow is an integrated framework providing end-to-end workflow for implementing and evaluating DNN workloads on digital CIM. It bridges compilation and simulation infrastructures with flexible instruction set architecture (ISA) design. The framework addresses CIM capacity constraints through advanced partitioning and parallelism strategies in the compilation flow.

title: Routability-aware Packing for High-density Nonvolatile FPGAs
problem: NVFPGAs with MLC NVMs achieve high logic density but suffer from severely degraded CLB intra-routability, causing long packing times in CAD flow.
method: Routability-aware re-pair stage adjusts LUT assignments to reduce congestion and improve intra-routability; exploits structural equivalence of MLC LUTs to eliminate redundant routing attempts during packing.

title: ZION: A Practical Confidential Virtual Machine Architecture on Commodity RISC-V Processors
problem: Existing RISC-V TEE architectures rely on process-level abstractions or custom hardware extensions, limiting compatibility and scalability for confidential virtual machine deployment on commodity RISC-V processors.
method: ZION combines Physical Memory Protection (PMP) with paging for scalable memory isolation, introduces a short-path CVM mode for efficient context switching via secure vCPU mechanisms, and uses a split-page-table-based mechanism for secure memory sharing with virtio devices while maintaining compatibility with commodity RISC-V hardware.

title: AsyncDIMM: Achieving Asynchronous Execution in DIMM-Based Near-Memory Processing
problem: DIMM-based near-memory processing (NMP) architectures cannot efficiently support asynchronous execution between host CPUs and near-memory accelerators (NMAs) because independent memory controllers on both sides cause memory bus contention and potential DRAM errors when issuing concurrent accesses. Existing designs resort to synchronous execution, wasting either host or NMA compute.
method: AsyncDIMM introduces three operational modes on existing memory buses: single access (host or NMA only), concurrent access, and seamless mode switching. An offload-schedule-return mechanism with explicit and implicit synchronization ensures correct memory access semantics across modes. Optimized timing constraints reduce offload latency; a locality-aware switch-recovery method minimizes mode-switch overhead; adaptive batching with timing-division multiplexing notifications improves return bandwidth. Hardware modifications are limited to conventional host and NMA memory controllers and validated on FPGA.

title: Learning-Aided Safe Controller Synthesis with Formal Guarantees via Vector Barrier Certificates
problem: Generating controllers for safety-critical systems with formal safety guarantees is challenging; machine learning provides good simulation performance but lacks formal verification of safety properties.
method: Hybrid approach combining reinforcement learning for controller synthesis with deep learning-aided vector barrier certificate generation. The method verifies candidate vector barrier certificates rather than directly generating verified ones, using low computational complexity verification and handling non-convex vector BC constraints without relaxation.

title: LIA: A Single-GPU LLM Inference Acceleration with Cooperative AMX-Enabled CPU-GPU Computation and CXL Offloading
problem: Single-GPU LLM inference is constrained by GPU memory capacity, forcing either expensive multi-GPU deployments or frequent CPU-GPU transfers over slow PCIe, which bottleneck both latency and throughput.
method: LIA is a single-GPU LLM inference framework that systematically offloads matrix computations to AMX-enabled CPUs (4th-gen Sapphire Rapids and 6th-gen Granite Rapids Xeon), reducing CPU-GPU transfers by keeping model parameters near the CPU. LIA introduces a memory-offloading policy that integrates CXL memory (as an affordable DRAM extension) with DDR memory to expand effective model capacity for throughput-oriented batch workloads. The system partitions transformer layer computations between CPU and GPU based on runtime latency/throughput objectives, using AMX tile instructions for high-throughput GEMM on the CPU side.

title: Fusion: An Analytics Object Store Optimized for Query Pushdown
problem: Disaggregated cloud storage uses erasure coding that partitions analytics file objects into fixed-size blocks across storage nodes; when query predicates are pushed down to storage (computation pushdown), the storage system must reassemble objects across nodes, incurring high network latency that undermines pushdown's intended benefits for ad-hoc and highly-selective OLAP queries.
method: Fusion is an analytics object store that co-designs storage layout and query pushdown execution for erasure-coded environments. It reorganizes how analytics file objects (e.g., Parquet files) are partitioned and distributed across storage nodes so that query-relevant data stripes can be accessed and evaluated locally at storage nodes without full object reassembly. Pushdown execution is coordinated across storage nodes in a way that respects erasure coding boundaries, enabling predicate evaluation close to data while minimizing cross-node communication.
